title: 45Z carbon intensity, field by field
summary: Break a producer's planting intentions into fields, estimate each field's 45Z carbon intensity (CI) score, and confirm it with the producer after harvest.

items.text: Each crop row now has a Fields line. Click Add field, then enter the field's CTRM split ID and a name. The fields break down the row's total acres.

Add the 45Z program to a field and enter its farming practices: yield, nitrogen, cover crop, tillage and manure. The field gets an estimated CI score from USDA's calculator, which updates as you type.
Already entered the same practices on another field? Use Copy to other fields… instead of typing them again.

After harvest, open Confirm CI Score and work through it with the producer: check the inputs, confirm the tillage with USDA's T-DISC check, pick the field's CTRM tickets and enter the actual yield, then confirm. The confirmed CI is the field's official 45Z result.
Download the Biofuel Feedstock Report (PDF) for a confirmed field, or the Mass Balance Ledger (CSV) for the producer.
A confirmed CI is locked. To change it, use Unlock to correct… and give a reason; the earlier result is kept in its history.

title: Producers straight from CTRM, and help inside the app
summary: Add a producer as soon as they are set up in CTRM, and get answers from a new Help panel on any page.

items.text: Producers now come from CTRM, the customer master, instead of the ODS. Names, addresses, contact details, NOP ID and ACH payment details are refreshed from CTRM every night.
Searching to add a producer now looks in CTRM directly, so a producer set up in CTRM today can be found and added right away, without waiting for the next day.

A new Help panel answers questions about the Workbench. Click the ? at the top right, next to your profile menu, then type a question or pick a suggestion. Answers include steps and buttons that take you straight to the right place.

Can't find a producer? Help searches every trade unit in the Workbench for them. If they aren't in the Workbench yet, it checks CTRM, so you can add them. Either way, it tells you where the producer is and how to open or add them.

Browse every help topic on the Help page, from Help in the profile menu. If you still need help, Still need help? gathers the details support asks for and walks you through opening a ServiceNow ticket.
A note on a producer with no trade unit could stop the Daily Recap going out to some groups. The recap now goes out as normal.
Notes on a producer with no trade unit are left out of the Daily Recap. Before adding a note, make sure the producer has a trade unit; you can check or add one in Edit Producer.

title: Bid sheets you can share, with bids fed from BarChart
summary: The Bid Sheet is rebuilt around named, shareable sheets of company-wide locations, and bids can now come straight from BarChart.

items.text: Bid sheets are now named working sets of locations. Create a sheet, add locations from the map or the picker, and share it with a desk, a group or a recap group. Several sheets can be open at once.
Locations are company-wide: one row per elevator, no longer tied to a trade unit. You can give a location your own display name on a sheet without changing it for anyone else.

The grid shows delivery months only, across several crop years at once, with the crop year and the futures board on each column header. The Yearly column is gone; a Yearly bid you had typed now sits on the month its basis letter names.
Show cash, basis or both. The choice is remembered for you and carries to the map, the bids popup and print. A positive basis shows with a leading +.
Pick which columns Edit Bids shows from its header, and export the grid to Excel. Edit Bids refreshes itself, so the header refresh button is gone.
On the map, All locations browses every elevator in the catalog. Clicking a pin shows that location's published bids, filtered by the chosen crop.

Add from BarChart: search by name, town, state or zip, tick several locations and add them in one go. Their bids come from the BarChart feed, carry the board symbol, fill every month the bid covers, and refresh daily.
A green Feed chip marks a fed bid and a blue Manual chip one you typed. You can override a fed bid by hand until the feed's next run.

title: Bin sites with grain on farm, and search by email
summary: Record a producer's bin sites and the grain stored at each one, and find producers by email.

items.text: A producer's page now lists their bin sites under Contact and Locations: a name, the capacity, and an optional map location that opens in Google Maps. Add or change them in Edit Producer.

Grain on farm is now recorded at a bin site. In Edit Producer, add a site, then add the crops stored there with bushels on hand, bushels sold, grade, target price and last bid. The producer's page groups the grain by site.

The producer-level Bin Capacity field is gone. Any capacity or grain on farm entered before this release was moved onto a bin site named Bin 1, so nothing was lost; rename it when you next edit the producer.

A new Grain on Farm & Bin Sites group of prompts finds producers by what they have on farm. Each result shows the producer's bin sites with the grain at each one, and any notes that mention a bin site by name. The refine filters cover every bin site and grain on farm field.
When a note mentions one of the producer's bin sites by name, the name shows in blue, and the note appears with that producer in Build a List.
You can now find a producer by their email address.
Anyone with access to the usage dashboard can now pick a manager and see the people who report to them. It starts on whoever is signed in.
Lists and insights built from contracts now load faster for large trade units.

title: Contracts and tickets now come straight from CTRM
summary: Contracts, pricing and tickets now come straight from CTRM, Scoular's contract system, instead of a copy of it.

items.text: Contracts, pricing and tickets now come straight from CTRM, Scoular's contract system, instead of a copy of it. Lists and insights built from contracts or tickets, such as the Unconfirmed Contracts and Unshipped Bushels cards or a Build a List prompt about contracts or deliveries, can take up to a minute the first time you open them for a trade unit; after that they are quick for as long as you keep working. Everything else loads as before.
If CTRM is slow or unavailable, the screen now says so and asks you to retry, instead of showing an empty list that looks like there is nothing there.

title: An organic badge, addresses in Google Maps, and planting by trade unit
summary: Organic producers are easy to spot, addresses open in Google Maps, and planting acres count under the trade unit you choose.

items.text: Organic producers now show an Organic Producer badge next to their name. Click it to see their NOP ID.
Click a producer's address to open it in Google Maps. The address now includes the ZIP code.
Trade unit names now come from Trade Unit Preferences, so they match the names set there instead of an older list that could be out of date.

When you add a planting intention you now choose which of the producer's trade units it is for, and the dashboard counts those acres only there. A producer on two trade units no longer has their acres counted under both.

The producer's planting table now has a Trade Unit column in place of Created On, and you can move a row to another trade unit when you edit it. Entries made before this release for producers on two trade units may be on the wrong one, so check those rows.
When you remove a producer from a trade unit that has planting intentions, you are asked where those acres should count instead.

Grain on farm is now recorded by specific commodity, such as HRWW or SRWW, using the same list as planting intentions. Existing entries keep their crop group, such as Wheat, until you edit them and pick the commodity.

title: Follow-ups, Teams channels, and lists that follow your trade units
summary: Set your own reminders on a producer, send a note straight to a Teams channel, and find your saved lists where you expect them.

items.text: You can set a follow-up on a producer and see it on their page under My Follow-Ups. These are private to you, and nobody else can see them.
Each follow-up also goes on your Outlook calendar, with a reminder the day before, so you get a nudge without having to come back into the app.

A producer with a follow-up coming up shows a clock on the producer list, colour-coded by how soon it is due. Build a List has a new Follow-Ups Scheduled card that pulls up everyone you owe a follow-up.

Typing @ in a note now offers the Teams channels you belong to, as well as people. Pick one and the note is posted straight to that channel. A channel only appears in the list if it has an email address set up in Teams — open the channel, choose Get email address, and it will show up here.

A Daily Recap group can be pointed at a Teams channel instead of email. Mention that group in a note and it posts to the channel rather than mailing everyone. Set it up under Manage Groups, using the channel email address.

A saved list now shows up whenever any one of its trade units is selected, instead of only when your selection matched exactly. Lists saved across two trade units used to disappear when you looked at one of them on its own.
Re-saving a list while a different trade unit was selected could permanently drop producers you had added by hand. Those producers are now kept.

The Crops filter now lists specific commodity codes rather than broad crop groups, so you can separate HRWW from SRWW instead of getting all wheat at once. You can still narrow by state in the same panel.

Organic and identity-preserved crops now show under their own names, such as Organic Soybeans and Waxy Corn, instead of being counted as the conventional crop. This applies to the Planting Intentions dashboard, the producer's planting table and the print report, and their acres and coverage are now measured against their own contracts. Existing entries pick this up on their own.
After each release the app tells you what changed, once. You can reopen it any time from the What's New row in your profile menu.
Your profile menu now shows which release and build you are on. Quote that line when you report a problem and we can tell exactly what you were running.
